paragraphs.source_en: Meanwhile, news of the counterrevolution had incited Turks, Kurds, Circassians, and Muslim refugees in the southern Anatolian city of Adana to express their anti-CUP feelings by massacring tens of thousands of Armenians with the complicity of local governmental and army officials. Local notables and religious students in Adana and the surrounding region opposed the new visibility of Armenian political parties and cultural institutions, which they blamed on the reinstitution of the constitution and parliament. Despite the complete destruction of the Armenian quarter of the city and many adjacent Armenian villages, the CUP Saving the Dynasty from Itself 4ll responded leniently towards the main culprits, not wishing to exacerbate hostility against itself.

paragraphs.source_en: Nevertheless, in the wake of the massacres in Adana and surrounding region, on 20 August 1909 the newly appointed interior minister Mehmed Talat and the CUP signed an accord with the Armenian Revolutionary Federation to cooperate ‘to save the Ottoman fatherland from separation and division’ and to defend the constitution against reactionaries.*° The CUP was deeply shaken by the counterrevolution and used it as a pretext to restrict the freedoms granted by the constitution, thereby strengthening the party’s grip over the empire. The counterrevolution confirmed CUP leaders’ belief that Muslim ‘reactionaries’ were among their greatest enemies. Within days of the surrender of the rebels, the parliament—representing the nation, the will of the people—deposed Abdiilhamid IL.
